summary: This lecture from Zadul-Ma'ad Part 99 covers the Year of Sadness (Year 10 of the Prophethood) when the Prophet Muhammad lost both his uncle Abu Talib and his first wife Khadijah. Sh. Ali Mashhour explains Abu Talib's unique position—he believed in the Prophet's truthfulness and prophethood but refused to publicly accept Islam due to fear of social consequences, illustrating the Islamic distinction between linguistic belief and legislative belief (amen). The lecture explores how belief requires both internal conviction and external adherence through actions and obedience. It also discusses the different ranks of believers, particularly the status of Siddiq (one who never experiences doubt), and how Khadijah held this rank. Sh. Ali Mashhour explains the critical loss of Abu Talib's protection, which forced a strategic change in the Prophet's approach to preaching.
